classifications.rationale: FocusTrace has no dedicated rule limiting exposed banner landmarks to one.
FocusTrace has no dedicated rule limiting exposed contentinfo landmarks to one.
FocusTrace reports multiple exposed main landmarks for structural review, but intentionally retains contextual REVIEW semantics.
FocusTrace reviews whether a page exposes a primary main landmark, sharing the same structural goal while retaining contextual outcome semantics.
FocusTrace checks repeated navigation, complementary and search landmarks for distinguishable names, but it does not yet cover every landmark role and axe uniqueness condition.
FocusTrace evaluates observed text-resize behavior but does not currently inspect meta viewport user-scalable or maximum-scale directives against the five-times zoom best-practice threshold.
FocusTrace reviews heading order but does not currently require a page or frame to contain a level-one heading.
FocusTrace can report ARIA properties unsupported by a presentational role, but it does not implement axe's complete global-ARIA/tabindex conflict and role-repair expectation.
FocusTrace can review main and repeated landmarks but does not currently require all page content to be contained by landmarks.
FocusTrace does not yet validate table scope attribute values and placement.
FocusTrace reviews availability of practical bypass mechanisms, including skip-link evidence, while axe specifically validates skip-link focus targets.
FocusTrace detects positive tabindex and reports it for contextual focus-order review; axe treats the same syntax as a best-practice failure.
FocusTrace does not compare table caption text with legacy summary text.
